context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 22 February 1899], Monte Carlo. Four days after thanking Harris for the money. He has been turned out of the Hotel Terminus at Nice — the English guests objected to his presence — and has pawned his ring for ten francs to get to Monte Carlo. The letter then itemises the whole Riviera arrangement back to Napoule.
quote:
Hôtel Terminus & Cosmopolitain, Monte Carlo

My dear Frank — I am in great trouble, and am obliged to come over to Monte Carlo and see you.

As I was, of course, unable to leave the hotel at Nice — not having enough money to pay the [inserted: whole] bill last Saturday — I have been forced to stay on, and to have my meals at table-d’hôte — though naturally at a separate table.

The middle-class English who are at the hotel have objected to my presence — and this morning I was presented with my bill and requested to leave by 12. o’c.

I declined to do this, and said I could not pay the bill today — They have given me till tomorrow at noon — and have asked me not to have my meals in the hotel — so I have come over to Monte Carlo, having raised 10 francs on my ring —

You have not forgotten that you invited me to spend three months on the Riviera as your guest — my bill at Napoule for eight weeks amounted to £35 — of which you gave me £30 — and I cannot think that it was very extravagant of me — the choice of Napoule was yours — and £4 a week is not very extravagant. Of course at Nice it is different. My bill is 40 francs a day at the hotel — you asked me to go there, and to look out for a villa for you. My one anxiety has been to leave the place, but I have not been able. Now I am turned out — and everyone at the hotel knows it — my dear Frank! you must come down and see me here for a few moments. You cannot, and you will not, abandon me — I won’t go to the Palace, because it would not be good for your Hotel for me to be seen there — this little place is quiet — Please come.

Ever yours O. W.
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 58-59 - one bifolium of illustrated Hotel-Cafe-Restaurant Terminus & Cosmopolitain, Monte-Carlo paper: image 58 shows sides 4 (left) and 1 (right), image 59 the inner opening, sides 2 and 3, with the letterhead showing through mirrored. Emphasis: none across the four sides, a null finding. The volume's only italic is 'table-d'hote', which is not underlined - its French convention again. Insertion: '[inserted: whole]' in the first paragraph, at 'not having enough money to pay the whole bill'. Read at 2.9x. Unusually it is written below the line rather than above, with a caret pointing up into the gap between 'the' and 'bill'. The volume prints the sentence complete and says nothing of the insertion. Punctuation: his dashes restored throughout, and they carry most of the letter; the volume converts them to full stops. '12. o'c.' and the figures '10 francs', '40 francs' are his, expanded to 'twelve o'clock', 'ten francs' and 'forty francs' in the volume. Crop warning, twice over: this letter runs from p. 1125 well onto p. 1126, and the printed page gives no signal of it. Render the whole page, or check the foot of it, before claiming the edition drops anything.
